issues.display_title: Issue #7: Admin API Key Security, Validation, and Tooling
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Currently, ADMIN_API_KEY is loaded directly as a string from environment variables without validation or management tooling:

  • If unconfigured or empty, admin endpoints return a 503 error without helpful setup guidance or CLI tooling to generate a secure key.
  • There is no startup validation or minimum entropy/length check when running in production environments.
  • There is no rate limiting or brute-force protection on the X-Admin-Key header authentication.

Proposed Solution

Enhance security and developer experience around ADMIN_API_KEY:

  • Provide a CLI helper command or script (e.g. python -m app.core.security generate-key) to generate cryptographically secure keys (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)).
  • Add validation during settings initialization: enforce or warn if ADMIN_API_KEY is too short or insecure when not in development environment.
  • Document best practices for key generation, configuration, and rotation in docs/ or README.md.

Design

  • Security Utility: Add a key generation utility using Python's secrets module.
  • Config Validation: In app/core/config.py, validate admin_api_key length and complexity when app_environment == "production".
  • Safe Feedback: Ensure 401 / 503 responses remain opaque and never leak secret expectations or system paths.

Acceptance Criteria

  • CLI/utility available to generate a secure random admin key
  • Minimum key length validation/warning in production mode
  • Documentation updated in README or docs/ explaining how to set up and rotate ADMIN_API_KEY
  • Existing admin authentication behavior remains backward-compatible
  • Automated tests for config validation and key generation utility

Result

  • Implemented CLI key generator tool (python -m app.core.security generate-key) generating cryptographic keys (secrets.token_urlsafe(32)).
  • Added settings validation in app/core/config.py enforcing minimum 32-character ADMIN_API_KEY length in production environment.
  • Updated README.md with guidelines on generating, configuring, and rotating admin API keys.
  • Added comprehensive unit tests in tests/core/test_security_and_config.py.
  • Merged via PR #13.

issues.display_title: Issue #8: Enhancement: Upload Action Granular Validation and Overwrite Control
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

The current POST /actions endpoint has usability and reliability limitations:

  1. Implicit Overwriting: The endpoint automatically and silently overwrites existing action documents with the same slug. There is no protection against accidental overwrites or option to reject/confirm before replacing an existing action.
  2. Orphan Files on 503 / Failure: When an upload request fails with HTTP 503 (e.g. unconfigured service, reload failure, or downstream error), the .md file can end up already written to the actions/ directory without proper cleanup/rollback, leaving behind orphan files in the filesystem.

Proposed Solution

Enhance POST /actions with overwrite protection and strict cleanup:

  • Overwrite Flag / Guard: Add an optional overwrite: bool = True parameter (or query param/form field) that returns 409 Conflict if the file already exists and overwrite is explicitly disabled (overwrite=false).
  • Guaranteed Cleanup / Rollback on 503 & Failures: Ensure that if any step fails (including 503 Service Unavailable, ingestion failure, or reload error), newly created files are strictly removed and existing files restored so no orphan .md file remains in actions/.

Design

  • Route: POST /actions
  • Parameters:
    • action: UploadFile (multipart)
    • overwrite: bool = Form(True)
  • Error Responses:
    • 409 Conflict: Return conflict when overwrite=False and actions/{slug}.md already exists.
    • 503 / 500 Failures: Ensure any failure guarantees rollback/cleanup of the uploaded file.
  • Rollback: Strengthen atomic write and restore mechanism so that no .md remains in actions/ on failure.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Overwrite flag honored: setting overwrite=false on an existing slug returns 409 Conflict without modifying the file
  • On 503 (or any other failure during reload/persistence), ensure uploaded file does not remain in actions/
  • Default behavior remains backward compatible
  • Automated tests added to tests/api/test_upload_action.py for overwrite guards and 503 cleanup verification

Result

  • Added overwrite parameter (bool = Form(True)) to POST /actions returning 409 Conflict if the action already exists and overwrite=False.
  • Implemented robust atomic rollback and cleanup preventing orphan .md files in actions/ when 503/500 reload errors occur.
  • Maintained backward compatibility for existing upload clients (overwrite=True by default).
  • Added comprehensive unit tests in tests/api/test_upload_action.py.
  • Merged via PR #14.

issues.display_title: Issue #9: Feature: View Detail Action File Endpoint
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Administrators can list action files via GET /actions, but cannot view the full markdown content and details of a specific action file via the API.

Proposed Solution

Add a GET /actions/{slug} endpoint to retrieve the raw markdown content and metadata for a specific action file.

Design

  • Route: GET /actions/{slug}
  • Auth: X-Admin-Key header required
  • Model: ActionDetailResponse
    • file_name: str
    • title: str
    • content: str
    • created_at: str (ISO 8601 UTC)
    • updated_at: str (ISO 8601 UTC)
  • Behavior:
    • Validates slug and prevents path traversal (e.g., ../)
    • Reads actions/{slug}.md (or matches filename)
    • Returns 404 Not Found if file does not exist
  • Errors: 401 Unauthorized, 404 Not Found, 503 Service Unavailable

Acceptance Criteria

  • GET /actions/{slug} returns full file content and metadata
  • Path traversal attempts return 400 Bad Request or 404 Not Found
  • Protected by X-Admin-Key header authentication
  • Unit/integration tests added in tests/api/test_detail_action.py
  • All test suites pass

Result

  • Implemented GET /actions/{slug} endpoint returning file metadata (file_name, title, created_at, updated_at) and raw markdown content.
  • Added slug validation and path traversal protection against malicious input patterns.
  • Secured endpoint with X-Admin-Key header authentication.
  • Added comprehensive unit and integration tests in tests/api/test_detail_action.py.
  • Merged via PR #11.

issues.display_title: Issue #10: Feature: Batch Upload Actions Endpoint
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Currently, adding multiple custom action files requires calling POST /actions multiple times, causing repeated full RAG index reloads and slower bulk ingestion.

Proposed Solution

Add a POST /actions/batch endpoint accepting multiple markdown files in a single request, performing per-file validation, atomic filesystem writes, and a single RAG index reload.

Design

  • Route: POST /actions/batch
  • Auth: X-Admin-Key header required
  • Parameters:
    • actions: list[UploadFile] (multipart)
    • overwrite: bool = Form(True)
  • Response: BatchActionUploadResponse
    • total: int
    • succeeded: list[ActionFileInfo]
    • failed: list[BatchErrorItem] (filename, reason)
    • documents_loaded: int
  • Behavior:
    • Validates each .md file structure (Title, Purpose, UI Flow)
    • Saves valid files to the actions/ directory
    • Runs a single reload for indexer and retriever
    • Performs cleanup/rollback on critical failures

Acceptance Criteria

  • POST /actions/batch accepts multiple markdown files
  • Handles overwrite protection per file based on overwrite flag
  • Performs a single RAG index reload after writing all files
  • Returns structured response detailing succeeded and failed files
  • Protected by X-Admin-Key header authentication
  • Unit/integration tests added in tests/api/test_batch_upload_actions.py
  • All test suites pass

Result

  • Implemented POST /actions/batch endpoint supporting bulk markdown action uploads via multipart form.
  • Added per-file overwrite protection using overwrite boolean parameter and per-file error handling with structured reporting.
  • Optimized RAG index reloading to execute once per batch request instead of per file.
  • Added atomic rollback support restoring/cleaning up written files on critical reload failures.
  • Added test coverage in tests/api/test_batch_upload_actions.py.
  • Merged via PR #12.
